messages:
sasha: R12 is seeing repeated NIC resets and subsequent GPU slab evictions. Dedicated tenants hitting warm-pool prefill failures. Seeing 'vf_reset' on eth0 and GPU slab reclaim logs. Anyone oncall?

jamie: On it. Can you paste the last 2m of node logs (r12-n3,n4,n7)?

sasha: Here are the tail lines from r12-n3 (pulled 17:14 UTC):
```
[17:12:58] eth0: VF 2 reset triggered by vf_reset_handler
[17:13:01] eth0: DMA burst exceeded threshold: 256MB in 3s
[17:13:03] kernel: GPU slab reclaim: evicting 256MB from slab 0x7f9
[17:13:03] kubelet: pod prefill failed: warm-pool coldstart
[17:13:05] eth0: VF 3 reset triggered by vf_reset_handler
```
Affected nodes: r12-n3, r12-n4, r12-n7.

theo: This pattern looks like NIC driver resets under sustained DMA bursts. We saw similar with MTU=9000 + fq_codel qdisc change. Did anything change in r12 recently?

anika: We rolled a kernel-touch hotfix (~5.10.72) to r12 yesterday at 02:15 UTC (rolled only r12 to test). Could be a regression.

miko: Rolling back kernel on a rack will disrupt workloads. If we need immediate mitigation I'd prefer to cordon R12 for new allocations and shift affected dedicated tenants to fallback pools first.

ryland: Heads up on cost: spilling dedicated tenants cross-az or to reserved fallback will increase egress and reserved capacity. Ballpark +$3k/day if this is sustained for a full day. Approve if it's the safer route.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0921-1147 — paging oncall eng-infra.

jamie: Actioned: cordoned r12 for new allocations (no new pods). Also probing MTU -> setting MTU=1500 on r12-n3,r12-n4,r12-n7 as a quick test.

sasha: After MTU change on r12-n3 we saw an immediate drop in vf_reset events (17:16 UTC). r12-n7 still shows slab evictions and vf_resets intermittently.

theo: r12-n7 telemetry shows sustained high DMA from tenant 'vision-stable' (bulk preproc). It's hammering NIC leading to resets and then triggering slab churn on the GPU host. Can we throttle that tenant at proxy/ingress?

anika: I just applied a per-tenant egress cap for vision-stable to 200Mbps at the edge proxy. Also temporarily disabled preemption for dedicated pools in that AZ to avoid slab churn while we triage.

ryland: Throttling is fine but ops wants customer comms. Also we should schedule a rollback of the 5.10.72 hotfix tonight if more signs point to regression — propose 23:00 UTC 3hr window.

miko: I'll handle customer notifications and the maintenance page. Rollback plan: node-by-node reboot/rollback to 5.10.69, drain with warm-pool-preserve flag off -> this needs a 2h coordinated window to avoid causing mass cold starts.

sasha: Summary / next steps:
- Keep R12 cordoned for new allocations (jamie) :thumbsup:
- Monitor VF reset counts and slab eviction rates (sasha/jamie)
- Throttle vision-stable egress to 200Mbps (anika) — done
- Schedule rollback maintenance at 23:00 UTC if telemetry doesn't stabilize (miko)
- Prepare cost/egress estimate for potential 24h spill (ryland)
Will post updates in thread.

jamie: Quick probe result: MTU change reduced resets on n3/n4, n7 still problematic — likely tenant-induced. Continuing to tail logs.

sasha: Thanks all. If anyone sees repeat vf_resets spike again, tag me and ops-bot.

miko: Noted. I'll open a runbook for the rollback and draft the customer note now.
